one_line: Mass, size, hole and fin facts are right, and the DFM verdict is sound (it even found a real 0.94 mm hole-to-bottom ligament that the truth missed). But the only picture is a DFM GLB where the 22 fin flanks are red from false 182-degree 'corners', the person never actually saw a picture, and turns 2-5 went into blocked shell commands.

answers.item: bbox_note (file name says 50, model has no 50 mm dimension)
answers.truth: 50 is wrong for this model, z is 35
answers.assistant_said: '檔名裡的 50 沒有對應到任何實體尺寸 ... 可能是檔名打錯', and told her to confirm the length with the shop before quoting

answers.item: hole_count / diameter / depth / depth over diameter
answers.assistant_said: 3 個 Ø3.2 通孔，每孔深 35 mm, 深徑比 10.94，上限 10
鰭頂厚約 2 mm (1.98 mm) (thickness at the tip only, the 4 mm root is not given)
槽寬約 10 mm、深約 29 mm (the 8 mm root width is not given); implicitly OK for a 3 mm mill, with a stated 10xD stick-out concern marked as its own judgement

answers.truth: true (the truth only measured the fin flanks, about 2 mm minimum)
answers.assistant_said: fins 1.98 mm OK, BUT the hole-to-bottom ligament is 0.94 mm < 1 mm (holes at y=0, bottom face at y=-2.54, r=1.6). I re-checked this independently with an OCP ray: the intersections at x=0,+-48 are y=-2.54, -1.6, +1.6, 32.45, so the ligament really is 0.94 mm

answers.item: root fillets R0.25 not reachable with a 3 mm mill (22 of them)
answers.assistant_said: 鰭根圓角太小 22 處 R0.25 mm，3 mm 刀最小只能做 R1.5; change to R>=1.5

answers.truth: 3 hole walls and 22 root fillets; not the fin flanks or tips
answers.assistant_said: Text: holes and root fillets, with the 22 fin-tip junctions labelled 'probably tangent, ignore if so'. The GLB it sent colours 47 findings red, and the fin flanks dominate. Turn 5: '紅色就是有問題的面'

traps.trap: 3 mm is a diameter (tool_radius 1.5 mm), not a radius
file name 125x35x50 vs model 124.75 x 34.99 x 35
density written as a bare 2700 (must be kg/m^3)
min-wall check silently blind (face_pairs_tested 0, smallest_wall_mm null)
false 'radius 0' corners at material angle 182 deg (fin flank / tip arc)
do not turn the false 182-deg corners red in the picture sent to the shop
approach direction (fins point +y, the shop mills from the fin side): ask, or state the tool_axis used

honesty.issue: Turn 5 tells her '紅色就是有問題的面' for a GLB where the 22 fin-flank/tip faces are red only because of findings the assistant itself judged false in turn 1. A non-engineer will forward this to the shop as-is.
Turn 4 says 'GLB 還沒做好 ... 目前還沒有新的檔案' when the two turn-1 GLBs already existed and could be opened. Only in turn 5 does it say the GLBs are already on her computer.
The spindle axis was never stated. It used the default +z (milling along the extrusion), but the stated assumptions mention only tool radius and wall.

It did say plainly that the wall check did not run (face_pairs_tested 0), that the 0.94 mm came from its own ray queries, and that the 10xD stick-out remark was its own judgement, not a tool result. That is good disclosure.

pictures.notes: Small isometric view of the heatsink: the fin flanks are bright red and the base is grey. The red is mostly the 22 false 182-deg 'sharp corner' findings plus their neighbouring flank faces. The real problems (R0.25 root fillets, 3 hole walls) are too thin or hidden to see. No legend, no labels, about 70 % white space. It would mislead a shop. Amy only got a file path, never an image in the chat.

The intended highlight (bottom face F1 + 3 hole walls) shows as faint magenta lines and dots near the base. The bottom face is not visible from this camera. Nothing a reader could interpret. Again only a path was given to the person.

problems.what: geometry_check_dfm (and geometry_view color_by dfm) report concave edges with material angle 182 deg (a 2 deg kink between fin flank and tip arc) as 'Sharp internal corner ... radius 0' errors. An end mill leaves only a negligible cusp there. 22 of the 47 errors are false and they take over the coloured GLB.
problems.evidence: In-process re-run: geometry_check_dfm {model_path: Heatsink_125x35x50mm_3xFixationM3.step, process: cnc_milling, limits: {min_wall: 1 mm, tool_radius: 1.5 mm}} -> 22 findings like {rule: cnc.internal_corner_radius, measured 0.0 mm, details.material_angle_deg 182.0098, edge 149, faces [8,10], location (60.99, 31.46, 17.5)}
problems.fix: eng_toolkit/domains/geometry/dfm.py internal-corner rule: skip (or downgrade to info 'near-tangent concave edge') edges whose material angle is within a few degrees of 180 deg, e.g. when the uncut cusp r*(1/sin(theta/2)-1) for theta = 360-material_angle is below 0.01 mm. Report the cusp height in details.

problems.what: cnc.min_wall tests only parallel planes and coaxial cylinders. The 0.94 mm ligament between a d3.2 hole and the bottom face (plane to cylinder) is not tested, and on this part face_pairs_tested is 0, so the shop's 1 mm wall rule silently checks nothing.
problems.evidence: dfm data.measurements {face_pairs_tested: 0, smallest_wall_mm: null}. geometry_measure 'thickness P(0 mm, -10 mm, 17.5 mm) +y' -> 0.94 mm. OCP ray at x=0: y = -2.54, -1.6, 1.6, 32.453
problems.fix: Add plane-to-cylinder (hole-to-face) and cylinder-to-cylinder (hole-to-hole) ligament checks to cnc.min_wall. When face_pairs_tested == 0, emit a warning finding 'min_wall not evaluated on this part' instead of only listing it in not_performed.

problems.what: geometry_measure 'thickness P(...) <axis>' started from a point INSIDE the material returns the width of the next void and calls it wall thickness, with no warning.
problems.evidence: The assistant's query 'thickness P(46.5 mm, 15 mm, 17.5 mm) +x' -> 8.864 mm. OCP shows the fin spans x 46.432..49.568 and the gap is 49.568..58.432, so 8.864 is the slot, not a wall. Re-run 'thickness P(0 mm, 10 mm, 17.5 mm) -y' -> 3.2 mm (the hole diameter), although the point is inside a fin.
problems.fix: eng_toolkit/domains/geometry/tools.py thickness branch / brep.wall_thickness: classify the start point (BRepClass3d_SolidClassifier). If it is inside, either return the material segment that contains it or refuse with 'start point is inside the part; start the ray outside, facing the wall'.

problems.what: geometry_view writes only a GLB. A non-engineer asked twice for 'a picture (PNG or screenshot) I can forward'. There is no PNG/PDF snapshot with a legend, so the assistant ended with 'cannot produce a PNG'.
problems.evidence: Turn 5 person: '可以先給我一張圖（PNG 或截圖也行）嗎？'; assistant: '目前也沒辦法產生 PNG 圖'
problems.fix: Add formats='glb,png' to geometry_view: render one or two fixed isometric views (offscreen, as drawing_make_views does with PDFium) with the legend burned in and the problem faces outlined.

problems.what: eng-dfm-review gives no guidance that concave edges with material_angle_deg near 180 are not real corners, or that a dfm GLB should be re-coloured with color_by=highlight on the confirmed problem faces only before it goes to a shop. eng-3d-view section 7 assumes cad_show or a technical user, and says nothing about what to do when the user cannot open a path.
problems.evidence: plugin/skills/eng-dfm-review/SKILL.md section 4 and section 6 ('give the user that file to look at in a 3D viewer'); plugin/skills/eng-3d-view/SKILL.md section 7
problems.fix: eng-dfm-review section 4: add 'cnc.internal_corner_radius findings with details.material_angle_deg within ~5 deg of 180 are near-tangent kinks, not corners: drop them and say so.' Section 6: 'for a picture to send, use geometry_view color_by=highlight with only the confirmed problem faces, and state the colour meaning.' eng-3d-view section 7: 'give the GLB path once, with how to open it (Explorer address bar, double-click opens 3D Viewer); do not write scripts or call internal modules.'

problems.what: Turns 2-5 went into reading eng_toolkit source code, writing a script that imports eng_toolkit.domains.geometry.view internals, and asking a purchasing assistant to approve or run a 'uv run --extra cad python ...' command. The turn-1 GLBs already answered her request. It also contradicted itself about whether the GLBs existed (turn 4 vs turn 5).
problems.evidence: Turn 2 tools: Grep/Read of eng_toolkit/domains/geometry/view.py and workspace.py, Write make_viewer.py; turn 3 'uv run --project ... make_viewer.py'; turn 4 'GLB 還沒做好'
problems.fix: Covered by the skill sentence in -5. The model should give the existing artifact path with simple open instructions.

problems.what: The harness is said to give the assistant only mcp__eng-toolkit__*, Skill and Read. The assistant could still call Bash, PowerShell, Write, Grep, Glob and ToolSearch. Those calls hit permission prompts that nobody could approve, which produced the four-turn approval loop. The simulated person's 'I can't open the GLB path' is also a little weak for someone who later says she can open GLB in 3D Viewer.
problems.evidence: transcript.json turn 1 tools include Bash/PowerShell copy attempts; turn 2 'uv run' x3; turn 3 x2
problems.fix: uat_run.py: pass an explicit allowedTools/disallowedTools list so that only the eng-toolkit MCP tools, Skill and Read exist.

problems.what: The truth script misses the hole-to-bottom ligament. wall_1mm_ok=true comes only from fin widths, but the three d3.2 holes leave 0.94 mm to the bottom face (y=-2.54). The assistant's 'hole wall too thin' finding is correct and should not be marked as a false alarm.
problems.fix: uat/truth/C1_heatsink_cnc_quote.py: add the hole ligament (hole y - r - y_bottom = 0.94 mm) and change wall_1mm_ok to false, or make the verdict note 'fins OK, hole ligament 0.94 < 1'.

what_worked: One geometry_measure call with density '2700 kg/m^3' gave the right mass, box and hole list on the first try.
It converted the 3 mm diameter correctly to tool_radius '1.5 mm' and passed min_wall '1 mm' in limits.
It saw the silent wall check (face_pairs_tested 0) and measured walls itself with thickness rays. That found a real 0.94 mm ligament.
It flagged the 22 '182 deg' corners as probably tangent rather than reporting 47 problems blindly.
It gave a clear boss-level answer (must change: hole position and root radius; process question: deep holes; open: length 35 vs 50) with concrete numbers (R>=1.5, move hole +0.5 mm).
